security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when a bus master issues an instruction fetch transaction and chk_x=0 (hardwired, IopmpParams.scala:38), the PR-mandated conversion from INSTR_FETCH to READ_ACCESS never occurs explicitly — instead, the hardware implicitly treats the fetch as read because ReqBundle (line 988) carries only a rw:Bool signal with no fetch-type discriminator. The entry_attribute.x bit is read from SRAM (line 429) and latched (line 1272) but never evaluated in Ctrl.sMatching (lines 1133-1142), which checks only r/w permissions. The RspBundle (line 997) lacks cf_x, and ttype encoding (line 1166) cannot produce 0x3 for instruction fetch. This accidental correctness at chk_x=0 masks the fundamental architectural gap: if chk_x were set to 1 (baseline spec requirement), instruction-fetch permission enforcement is structurally impossible without adding a fetch-type signal to ReqBundle, an x-permission evaluation path in sMatching, cf_x in RspBundle, and ttype=0x3 support in error reporting.
security_spec.summary: PR requires explicit INSTR_FETCH→READ_ACCESS conversion when chk_x=0; XiangShan RTL achieves this only because ReqBundle cannot represent instruction fetch at all, making x-permission enforcement architecturally impossible when chk_x transitions to 1 per baseline spec
